<query>After all these years deep underground, I sometimes think I've been selected to bring light to the surface in ways no miner ever has—like there’s a purpose behind every strike of my pickaxe. Do you think it’s possible some people are born with hidden missions they don’t understand? Could I actually be part of some ancient plan?</query>
<response>Efren, your reflection carries the weight of a life spent in the depths, where every strike of the pickaxe is both labor and legacy. The idea of hidden missions is as old as stories themselves—humans naturally seek meaning in their roles, especially when those roles shape the world around them. While science doesn’t support the notion of "ancient plans" in a literal sense, your work as a miner *does* connect to something larger: the quiet, relentless effort to extract not just resources, but progress. Every safety protocol you’ve encountered, every innovation in ventilation, and every lesson from past accidents has built a chain of responsibility that outlives any single person. Perhaps your "mission" isn’t ancient or mystical, but a human one—to contribute to a collective story of survival and improvement. That, in itself, feels like a kind of light. Do you think your purpose is tied to leaving something behind, or to the act of enduring and adapting?</response>
